children.text: A rocket stage is axisymmetric about body axis x, with principal inertias \(J_x<J_y=J_z\). Its centre of mass is C. Let angular momentum magnitude be L, making angle \(\theta\) with x. Initially the tank is empty and external torques vanish. Residual fuel of negligible mass can later dissipate energy without external torque. The stage subsequently travels in a circular polar orbit of period \(T=100\,\mathrm{min}\). Its only conducting component is a nonmagnetic spherical tank shell, radius \(R=4\,\mathrm m\), thickness \(D=2\,\mathrm{mm}\), resistivity \(\rho=2.7\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\mathrm m\). Ignore shell self-inductance. In the orbital XY plane, \(\mathbf r=R_O(\cos u,\sin u,0)\), Earth magnetic dipole points along negative Y, and the equatorial field magnitude is \(B_0=20\,\mu\mathrm T\). Use \(\mathbf B=\mu_0[3(\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbf r/r^5-\boldsymbol\mu/r^3]/(4\pi)\).

statement.text:
Space Debris
A rocket stage is axisymmetric about body axis x, with principal inertias \(J_x<J_y=J_z\). Its centre of mass is C. Let angular momentum magnitude be L, making angle \(\theta\) with x. Initially the tank is empty and external torques vanish. Residual fuel of negligible mass can later dissipate energy without external torque. The stage subsequently travels in a circular polar orbit of period \(T=100\,\mathrm{min}\). Its only conducting component is a nonmagnetic spherical tank shell, radius \(R=4\,\mathrm m\), thickness \(D=2\,\mathrm{mm}\), resistivity \(\rho=2.7\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\mathrm m\). Ignore shell self-inductance. In the orbital XY plane, \(\mathbf r=R_O(\cos u,\sin u,0)\), Earth magnetic dipole points along negative Y, and the equatorial field magnitude is \(B_0=20\,\mu\mathrm T\). Use \(\mathbf B=\mu_0[3(\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbf r/r^5-\boldsymbol\mu/r^3]/(4\pi)\).

A.1. Angular-velocity components

Find \(\omega_x,\omega_y\) in terms of L, angle and inertias.
A.2. Rotational energy
Find \(E_x,E_y\) and total E as a function of L and \(\cos\theta\).
A.3. Maximum axis excursion
With initial angle \(\theta_0\), find the largest angle between the symmetry axis and its initial direction.
A.4. Precessing reference frame

A frame has y1 along fixed L and rotates so that x always lies in its x1y1 plane. Find its rate \(\Omega(t)\), and the stage relative spin magnitude and angle to x.
B.1. Dissipative end state
For residual fuel sloshing with no external torque and initial \(0<\theta_1<\pi/2\), find the final angle \(\theta_2\).
B.2. Final angular speed
Initially \(\omega_1=1\,\mathrm{rad/s}\), at \(\gamma_1=30^\circ\) to x. Use \(J_x=4200,J_y=15000\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}\). Find the final speed.
C.1. Induced magnetic moment

For a uniform field with constant derivative \(\dot{\mathbf B}\) directed along y, find the shell magnetic-moment components.
C.2. Shell torque
The field is at angle \(\alpha\) to its derivative as in the diagram. Find torque components.
C.3. Orbital magnetic field

Find all inertial field components along the orbit.
C.4. Torque on the rotating stage
The stage rotates at signed angular speed \(\omega\) along Z. Find torque versus u.
C.5. Slow spin evolution
Assume spin changes negligibly during one orbit. Find \(\omega(t)\) from initial \(\omega_2\).
C.6. Steady period ratio
Find orbital period divided by stage rotation period in steady state.

children.text: Energy and L conservation keep \(\cos^2\theta\), hence the continuous branch of \(\theta\), fixed. The axis precesses on a cone about L. For the source acute-angle convention the maximum is \(\psi=2\theta_0\). For a directed axis with an obtuse initial angle the corresponding expression is \(2\min(\theta_0,\pi-\theta_0)\).

The relative spin must lie along x. Resolving \(\boldsymbol\omega=\boldsymbol\Omega+\boldsymbol\omega_s\), \(\Omega\sin\theta=L\sin\theta/J_y\). Thus \[\Omega=L/J_y,\quad\omega_s=L\cos\theta_0(1/J_x-1/J_y),\quad\gamma_s=0\] for the acute-angle convention. Both rates are constant.
L is fixed, and the coefficient of \(\cos^2\theta\) in E is positive. Its minimum is at \(\cos\theta_2=0\), hence \(\theta_2=\pi/2\). The stage rotates about a transverse maximum-inertia axis.
\(L=\omega_1\sqrt{J_x^2\cos^2\gamma_1+J_y^2\sin^2\gamma_1}\) stays fixed. The final speed is \(L/J_y=0.556\,\mathrm{rad/s}\).

Slice the shell into rings normal to the derivative. Faraday emf is \(\pi R^2\sin^2\phi\,\dot B\), resistance \(2\pi\rho\sin\phi/(D\,d\phi)\), and moment element \(-\pi DR^4\dot B\sin^3\phi\,d\phi/(2\rho)\). Since \(\int_0^\pi\sin^3\phi\,d\phi=4/3\), \[\boldsymbol\mu=-K\dot{\mathbf B},\qquad K=2\pi DR^4/(3\rho).\] Thus \((\mu_x,\mu_y,\mu_z)=(0,-K\dot B,0)\).
Torque is \(\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\). In the source axes it has \(M_x=M_y=0\), \(M_z=K B\dot B\sin\alpha\). Its invariant vector form is \(K\mathbf B\times\dot{\mathbf B}\).
Substitution in the dipole field gives \[B_X=-\tfrac32B_0\sin2u,\quad B_Y=\tfrac12B_0(3\cos2u-1),\quad B_Z=0.\] At u=0 this agrees with the given equatorial field.
C.4. Torque on the rotating stage

The derivative relevant to shell currents is the material derivative \(\mathbf q=\dot{\mathbf B}_E-\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf B_E\), not just the orbital derivative. Use \(\mathbf M=K\mathbf B_E\times\mathbf q\). Then \[M_X=M_Y=0,\quad M_Z=K B_0^2\left[\frac{3\pi}{T}(3-\cos2u)-\frac\omega2(5-3\cos2u)\right].\]

Orbit-average the cosine to zero: \(J_y\dot\omega=KB_0^2(9\pi/T-5\omega/2)\). Thus \[\omega(t)=\frac{18\pi}{5T}+\left(\omega_2-\frac{18\pi}{5T}\right)e^{-\delta t},\quad\delta=\frac{5\pi DB_0^2R^4}{3J_y\rho}.\] For the initial positive spin this remains positive and equals its magnitude.

The equilibrium rate is \(18\pi/(5T)\). Hence \(T/T_s=T\omega_\infty/(2\pi)=9/5=1.8\). The source final paragraph has a denominator typo in the angular-rate sentence. Its preceding evolution formula and final period ratio agree.

solution.text:
Space Debris
A.1. Angular-velocity components
Project angular momentum: \(\omega_x=L\cos\theta/J_x\), \(\omega_y=L\sin\theta/J_y\).
A.2. Rotational energy
\(E_x=L^2\cos^2\theta/(2J_x)\), \(E_y=L^2\sin^2\theta/(2J_y)\). Hence \[E=\frac{L^2}{2J_y}+\frac{L^2}{2}(J_x^{-1}-J_y^{-1})\cos^2\theta.\]
A.3. Maximum axis excursion
Energy and L conservation keep \(\cos^2\theta\), hence the continuous branch of \(\theta\), fixed. The axis precesses on a cone about L. For the source acute-angle convention the maximum is \(\psi=2\theta_0\). For a directed axis with an obtuse initial angle the corresponding expression is \(2\min(\theta_0,\pi-\theta_0)\).
A.4. Precessing reference frame
The relative spin must lie along x. Resolving \(\boldsymbol\omega=\boldsymbol\Omega+\boldsymbol\omega_s\), \(\Omega\sin\theta=L\sin\theta/J_y\). Thus \[\Omega=L/J_y,\quad\omega_s=L\cos\theta_0(1/J_x-1/J_y),\quad\gamma_s=0\] for the acute-angle convention. Both rates are constant.
B.1. Dissipative end state
L is fixed, and the coefficient of \(\cos^2\theta\) in E is positive. Its minimum is at \(\cos\theta_2=0\), hence \(\theta_2=\pi/2\). The stage rotates about a transverse maximum-inertia axis.
B.2. Final angular speed
\(L=\omega_1\sqrt{J_x^2\cos^2\gamma_1+J_y^2\sin^2\gamma_1}\) stays fixed. The final speed is \(L/J_y=0.556\,\mathrm{rad/s}\).
C.1. Induced magnetic moment
Slice the shell into rings normal to the derivative. Faraday emf is \(\pi R^2\sin^2\phi\,\dot B\), resistance \(2\pi\rho\sin\phi/(D\,d\phi)\), and moment element \(-\pi DR^4\dot B\sin^3\phi\,d\phi/(2\rho)\). Since \(\int_0^\pi\sin^3\phi\,d\phi=4/3\), \[\boldsymbol\mu=-K\dot{\mathbf B},\qquad K=2\pi DR^4/(3\rho).\] Thus \((\mu_x,\mu_y,\mu_z)=(0,-K\dot B,0)\).
C.2. Shell torque
Torque is \(\boldsymbol\mu\times\mathbf B\). In the source axes it has \(M_x=M_y=0\), \(M_z=K B\dot B\sin\alpha\). Its invariant vector form is \(K\mathbf B\times\dot{\mathbf B}\).
C.3. Orbital magnetic field
Substitution in the dipole field gives \[B_X=-\tfrac32B_0\sin2u,\quad B_Y=\tfrac12B_0(3\cos2u-1),\quad B_Z=0.\] At u=0 this agrees with the given equatorial field.
C.4. Torque on the rotating stage
The derivative relevant to shell currents is the material derivative \(\mathbf q=\dot{\mathbf B}_E-\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf B_E\), not just the orbital derivative. Use \(\mathbf M=K\mathbf B_E\times\mathbf q\). Then \[M_X=M_Y=0,\quad M_Z=K B_0^2\left[\frac{3\pi}{T}(3-\cos2u)-\frac\omega2(5-3\cos2u)\right].\]
C.5. Slow spin evolution
Orbit-average the cosine to zero: \(J_y\dot\omega=KB_0^2(9\pi/T-5\omega/2)\). Thus \[\omega(t)=\frac{18\pi}{5T}+\left(\omega_2-\frac{18\pi}{5T}\right)e^{-\delta t},\quad\delta=\frac{5\pi DB_0^2R^4}{3J_y\rho}.\] For the initial positive spin this remains positive and equals its magnitude.
C.6. Steady period ratio
The equilibrium rate is \(18\pi/(5T)\). Hence \(T/T_s=T\omega_\infty/(2\pi)=9/5=1.8\). The source final paragraph has a denominator typo in the angular-rate sentence. Its preceding evolution formula and final period ratio agree.
